name: Ice Angels
howToApply: Pitch via Icehouse Ventures (Ice Angels operates within it) — start at their 'raise capital' page.
notes: NZ's largest angel network, 150+ members, NZ$65m+ invested in 100+ companies since 2003. Cheque range is from a third-party profile (individual cheques ~$25k–250k, syndicated rounds up to ~$1.5m) — confirm current figures directly.

name: Enterprise Angels
howToApply: Apply for funding through their website; deals also listed on their AngelEquity platform.
notes: 200+ investors; has facilitated $65m+ into 107 startups. Stage range inferred from public descriptions.

name: AngelHQ
howToApply: Submit your venture via their website for consideration at member pitch evenings.
notes: Wellington's angel club; has backed 180+ NZ companies. Stage range inferred.

name: Canterbury Angels
howToApply: Contact via the network's listing; deals often syndicate with other NZ angel groups.
notes: Listed among NZ angel networks; current activity level not independently confirmed — check before relying on this entry.

name: Otago Angels
howToApply: Managed from the Upstart incubator in Dunedin — approach via Upstart or the network directly.
notes: 90+ investors; publicly stated preference for deals in the $100k–$1m range.

name: Flying Kiwi Angels
howToApply: Offers free founder advice sessions — book one via their site as a first step.
notes: Founded 2014; ~50 investors including offshore members; reverse-sidecar investment model.

name: Angel Investors Marlborough
howToApply: Contact through their website.
notes: Founded 2017; Angel Association NZ member. Stage range inferred.

name: ArcAngels
howToApply: Female-led ventures can apply via their website; also runs the ArcAngels Fund.
notes: NZ's only angel network dedicated to female-led startups (founded 2013). ArcAngels Fund II is a $10m active early-stage fund; Fund I ($2.8m) backed 31 ventures.

name: Icehouse Ventures
howToApply: Apply through the 'raise capital' section of their website; runs dedicated seed funds (Seed Fund IV, $70m, ~30 new ventures).
notes: NZ$454m under management (Jan 2025); $800m+ invested into 390+ companies since 2003 including the Ice Angels era.

name: Movac
howToApply: Pitch via their website.
notes: One of NZ's largest and most established VCs; backed by NZGCP's Elevate fund-of-funds. Stage detail inferred — confirm current fund mandate.

name: GD1 (Global From Day One)
howToApply: Pitch via their website.
notes: Science-led NZ companies; Elevate-backed.

name: Blackbird (NZ)
howToApply: Open pitch submission via their website; seed-led AU/NZ fund with a dedicated NZ vehicle.
notes: Blackbird Ventures NZ appears in NZGCP Elevate's fund portfolio.

name: Outset Ventures
howToApply: Apply via their website; also offers incubation with in-house laboratories.
notes: Deep-tech VC + incubator; Fund II closed oversubscribed at NZ$41.5m (2025); 26+ startups backed.

name: Nuance Connected Capital
howToApply: Pitch via their website.
notes: NZ's first dedicated deep-tech VC fund (founded 2021); ~NZ$55m fund with a $17m NZGCP commitment.

name: Hillfarrance
howToApply: Pitch via their website; founder-aligned model that shares fund returns with portfolio founders.
notes: Pre-seed and seed specialist; Elevate-backed. Website URL not independently verified — confirm.

name: K1W1
howToApply: No public application process — typically reached via warm introduction or the Angel Association network.
notes: Sir Stephen Tindall's family office (est. 1999); $350m+ across ~175 companies (LanzaTech, Rocket Lab). No verified public website; stage range inferred.

name: NZGCP — Aspire NZ Seed Fund
howToApply: Aspire only co-invests alongside approved private investors (angel networks, seed funds) — so secure a private lead first; they bring Aspire in.
notes: Crown seed co-investment fund (est. 2006 as SCIF); weighting toward deep tech. Cheque range is from a third-party profile — confirm current settings; MBIE reviewed Aspire settings in 2025.

name: MBIE Innovation Services (ex-Callaghan Innovation grants)
howToApply: Browse current R&D and startup funding at funds.business.govt.nz; the R&D Tax Incentive continues under MBIE.
notes: Callaghan Innovation was disestablished 1 December 2025; grants and startup programmes moved to MBIE. Ārohia grants reportedly closed permanently (Dec 2025, third-party report) — check funds.business.govt.nz for what's currently open.

name: Te Puni Kōkiri — Māori Business Growth Support
howToApply: Apply via Te Puni Kōkiri (Pūtea Kimihia / Pūtea Tipuranga / Pūtea Whakaako) or the Māori Business Growth Fund on tupu.nz.
notes: Grants and support for Māori-owned businesses at early stages.

name: NZTE — Invest / Raise Capital support
howToApply: NZTE's investment team helps NZ companies prepare for and run capital raises (not a funder itself); free 'InvestEd' resources online.
notes: Capital-raising support and investor connections rather than direct capital. Invest New Zealand (new Crown entity, est. 1 July 2025) focuses on attracting international investment.

name: Snowball Effect
howToApply: Apply to raise on the platform; public offers can raise up to $2m/year from retail investors under NZ equity-crowdfunding rules, plus wholesale offers.
notes: FMA-licensed equity crowdfunding platform since 2014; active.

name: PledgeMe
howToApply: Apply to run an equity or project campaign on the platform.
notes: Wellington-based, est. 2011, FMA equity licence since 2014; active. (Equitise, the other platform founders may remember, had its FMA licence suspended in April 2024 and is not active in NZ.)

name: Catalist
howToApply: List on NZ's licensed growth stock exchange for SMEs/startups — public, wholesale and private market options with periodic auctions.
notes: Regulated marketplace (raises up to $20m/yr from the public); also publishes the annual NZ Angel Market Report.

name: Ministry of Awesome
howToApply: Apply to Founder Catalyst (incubation) or national accelerators including Electrify (women & non-binary founders) and the Orion Energy Accelerator.
notes: Ōtautahi Christchurch-based, ChristchurchNZ-funded; 'women' tag reflects the Electrify programme specifically.

name: Creative HQ
howToApply: Apply to current accelerator programmes via their website.
notes: Wellington innovation hub; 26 accelerators run since 2013 plus GovTech programmes.

name: Kōkiri
howToApply: Kaupapa Māori accelerator for Māori-led startups — apply via their website.
notes: Launched 2018 (Callaghan Innovation / Te Wānanga o Aotearoa / Creative HQ partnership); historically $10,000 + 12-week programme. Current status after Callaghan's Dec 2025 disestablishment unverified — confirm before applying.

name: Startmate (AU/NZ)
howToApply: Apply to the hybrid AU/NZ accelerator cohorts via their website.
notes: Australian accelerator with NZ cohorts and alumni (e.g. Cropsy, Komodo); current NZ cohort cadence unconfirmed.
